rule: Three questions per starter, never more. Answers fill the {{placeholders}}; everything else ships as written. The nine-question worksheet is the Version 2 step, offered after a week of use.

starters.title: Write like me
starters.oneLine: Drafts emails, notes, and posts that sound like you, then you edit.

questions.label: Who you are, in one sentence
questions.hint: Role and what you know a lot about. "Independent consultant to logistics companies, eleven years."

questions.label: Who usually reads what you write
questions.hint: "Owners and operations heads who've heard every pitch."

questions.label: Three words or phrases you never use
questions.hint: "Leverage. Circle back. I hope this finds you well."

starters.title: Check the facts before I send
starters.oneLine: Runs a seven-step pass on anything with a number, a name, a date, or a quote in it.

questions.label: What you send that has to be right
What a wrong fact costs you
questions.hint: "A client. A correction in front of the board."

questions.label: One thing it has gotten almost right before
questions.hint: "The date from the proposal instead of the final rule." Leave blank if none yet.

starters.title: My weekly report
starters.oneLine: The thing you write every week, drafted from your notes in the shape you'd write it.

questions.label: What the report is and who reads it
questions.hint: "Monday pipeline summary for my VP, read on her phone."

questions.label: Three things that must never appear
questions.hint: "Bullets. The word robust. A deal without a date."

starters.title: Research I can trust
starters.oneLine: Finds things out with a source and a date on every fact, and a line for what it couldn't verify.

questions.label: Your field, in a few words
questions.hint: "Nonprofit fundraising." "Commercial real estate in the Midwest."

questions.label: Three sources you trust in your field
questions.hint: "The funder's own reports. The national association. The agency's statistics."

questions.label: One kind of source it should never treat as a source

starters.title: Who my company is
starters.oneLine: Checks everything it makes for you against who you are, before colors and fonts.

questions.label: We are...
questions.hint: One sentence a customer would use. "Two accountants who answer the phone."

questions.label: We serve...
questions.hint: Who, and what they can't afford. "Owners who can't afford a surprise."

questions.label: We never...
questions.hint: One thing you won't do even when it would win. "Promise a result we don't control."

starters.title: My posts
starters.oneLine: Drafts a post that opens on a fact, holds one opinion, and has none of the tells. You post it.

questions.label: Where you post, and for whom
questions.hint: "LinkedIn, for other founders and the operators we sell to."

questions.label: How long a post of yours is
Three things you never do in a post
questions.hint: "Hashtags. Exclamation points. End on a question."
